analysis: The method parseInt0 takes a CharSequence sequence and indices p and lim. It calls sequence.charAt(p) twice: first to check for a negative sign, and then in a loop to parse digits. The charAt method throws IndexOutOfBoundsException if the index is negative or not less than the sequence length. The code does not validate that p >= 0 or that lim <= sequence.length(). The initial check only ensures p != lim, but does not check p against the sequence length. After incrementing p for a negative sign, there is a check if p >= lim, but again no check against sequence length. In the loop, p is incremented until p == lim, but if lim exceeds the sequence length, p may exceed sequence.length() - 1, causing an IndexOutOfBoundsException. Therefore, the throwing condition for IndexOutOfBoundsException is not avoided by any checks or validations in the given context.
answer: The only declared exception is IndexOutOfBoundsException. Its throwing condition is not avoided.
remark: IndexOutOfBoundsException can be triggered in two scenarios: (1) In the first call sequence.charAt(p), if p is negative or p >= sequence.length(). (2) In the loop call sequence.charAt(p), if during iteration p becomes greater than or equal to sequence.length() before reaching lim. This happens when lim is greater than sequence.length(), or when the initial p is already out of bounds, or when the sequence length is insufficient to cover the range [p, lim).
